reasoning: Both attempts produce a working panel with live data, correct strokes and gradients, and a correctly tiled hex pattern. A builds no UIShadow anywhere. It turns the panel drop shadow and the Selected glow into images and lists them in the asset doc. It fakes the text and inner shadows, uses no sprite sheet, and leaves the blur uncompensated. B builds every shadow natively with UIShadow (inset, text mode, glow). It puts the block art and icons on sprite sheets with all ids in one module, and its asset doc lists exactly the right three images. B's extra features are mild scope creep, but it matches the rubric far more closely.

criteria.note: The panel drop shadow (`PanelShadow` 9-slice) and the Selected glow (`SlotGlow`) are images, and the docs list them as uploads; text shadows are duplicate labels and the inner shadow is a fake shaded frame, so no UIShadow is used anywhere.
One ImageLabel with `ScaleType.Tile` and `TileSize = fromOffset(112,192)`, inside a CanvasGroup under Background and outside the Content UIListLayout.

Content uses a vertical UIListLayout with Padding 16 and UIPadding 24/28; the grid is a UIGridLayout with 96 cells and 12 gaps; the header is laid out by hand with positions instead of flex, and the footer label has a fixed width beside the 200x52 button.
BackgroundTransparency 0.08; Rotation 90 gradients on white bases; strokes are 2 Inner, 1 Inner and 3 Outer through BorderStrokePosition; radii are 16, 12 and 0.5 scale.

No UIShadow at all: the shadow and glow are images, text shadows are hard-offset copies with the blur dropped, the inner shadow is faked, and the blur is just left out at 0.08 rather than made more opaque.
InventorySlot takes `isSelected`/`isLocked` from BlockInventory and BlockPlacer, and locked art gets ImageTransparency 0.6; it is not a single state prop, but slots stay in place in the grid.

Exports are 2x and white-tinted, and the ids live in one module (`InventoryStyle.Asset`), but there are ten separate block images instead of a sprite sheet, and the shadow and glow images shouldn't exist.
Uses live data, the E key toggles the panel, Equip calls `BlockPlacer.setBlockType`, Background is Active so clicks don't place blocks, and all checks pass.
Every shadow goes through `Shadow.build` (UIShadow); only the hex tile, the block-art sheet and the icon sheet are images, and the docs list exactly those.
`HexPattern` ImageLabel uses Tile with `TileSize` 112x192 in offsets, sits as a sibling of Content (outside the UIListLayout), and is inset 2 px with its own UICorner of 14.

Content uses a vertical UIListLayout with Padding 16 and UIPadding 24/28; the header is anchored left and right, centered vertically; the grid is a UIGridLayout 96/12; the footer label is `1, -(200+16)` wide beside the 200-wide button.
Rotation 90 gradients on white bases; strokes are 2 Inner, 1 Inner and 3 Outer; radii are 16, 12 and a full radius for the close button; the 0.04 fill is a deliberate stand-in for the blur.

Panel shadow is (0,12) blur 32 at 0.55; the Equip shadow is Inset at 0.75 with offset -3; text shadows use Mode Text; the glow is a UIShadow on the slot with a spring fade; the fill is made more opaque instead of using a BlurEffect.

One Slot component with IsSelected/IsLocked (plus an extra IsPicked); InventoryScreen reads BlockInventory and BlockTypes; locked content transparency 0.6 is applied to the art and swatch; the grid keeps slots fixed.
2x exports under 1024; an 800x320 block sheet read with ImageRectOffset and ImageRectSize; a white icon sheet tinted with ImageColor3; all ids in InventoryAssets.luau.

Equip calls `BlockPlacer.setBlockType` and the panel is Active, and all checks pass; it does add unrequested extras (open button, hover, picked state, equip-state labels) and rewrites Screen.luau with module-level connections.

strengths: Clean, working panel driven by real data
Hex tile done correctly and clipped by a CanvasGroup
Correct stroke positions, gradients and transparencies
weaknesses: No UIShadow: the shadow and glow become images, and text and inner shadows are faked
No sprite sheet for the block art
The asset doc lists images that should be built natively
Background blur is not compensated for

strengths: UIShadow used correctly for the drop, inset, text and glow shadows
Sprite sheets for blocks and icons, with every id in one module
Asset doc lists only what really needs to be an image
Clean split between the pure panel and the data wiring (InventoryScreen)
weaknesses: Scope creep: open button, hover states, a picked variant
Bigger rewrite of Screen.luau than needed
UIShadow built with Instance.new behind a pcall (not Vide's create)
